facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 3-month history of intertrigo involving his groin
he had been treating with a combination of clotrimazole cream, 1%, and hydrocortisone cream, 1%
bright red, burning and painful nodules around his scrotum
Two symmetrical solitary erythematous nodules were present in the right and left inguinal folds adjacent to the scrotum
Epidermal ulceration overlying a diffuse dermal proliferation composed of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
Intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies present as basophilic, somewhat laminated intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies measuring 5-8 μm in diameter
Bodies highlighted with iron (Prussian blue) and calcium (Von Kossa) stains
Background population of many plasma cells and few neutrophils noted
Fungus culture: Negative
Atypical mycobacteria culture: Negative
Bacterial culture: Positive for E. coli
Medical history included prostate cancer, hypertension, anxiety disorder, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and diverticulosis

concepts.why: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and the histopathological examination results support this diagnosis
The positive bacterial culture for E. coli supports this diagnosis
The presence of plasma cells and neutrophils in the background population supports this diagnosis

rationales.F03: The presence of bright red, burning, and painful nodules around the scrotum is more typical of Malacoplakia and chronic inflammatory disease.
rationales.F04: The presence of symmetrical solitary erythematous nodules in the inguinal folds is more typical of Malacoplakia and chronic inflammatory disease.
rationales.F05: The histopathological finding of epidermal ulceration and diffuse dermal proliferation with histiocytes is highly suggestive of Malacoplakia.
rationales.F06: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies is a hallmark of Malacoplakia.
rationales.F07: The staining of bodies with iron and calcium is consistent with Malacoplakia.
rationales.F08: The background population of plasma cells and neutrophils is more typical of Malacoplakia and chronic inflammatory disease.
rationales.F11: The positive bacterial culture for E. coli suggests an E. coli infection, but the presence of other findings is more typical of Malacoplakia.
